title: Export manifest
description: The immutable record of one export: which approved revision, as which generation, assembled into which bundle under which export options, for which connectors. The router commits it as the outbox event's manifest in the same transaction as the approved publishable revision; the exporter hands it with its bundle to `deliver(manifest, bundle)` on every connector it names, and it is each connector's idempotency key. Ordering is the pair (generation, options_revision), compared in that order: a connector refuses a delivery whose pair is lower than what it already holds, so a late retry never overwrites newer material. At an equal pair, manifest_id and bundle.content_hash are the identity a connector compares: the same pair and identity is an export already applied (acknowledged without rewriting, e.g. after a lost receipt), and the same pair with a different identity is a conflict (docs/gen2/EXPORT-API.md §4). JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling values or a manifest with its predecessor: that approval.approved_revision equals source.revision, that the superseded pair is strictly lower, and that pairs strictly increase per topic are enforced where the manifest is stored (DDL outbox_events).

generation.description: The topic's approved-generation number: each approved publishable revision (a completion, an approved evidence correction, an approved checkpoint publication) is one generation. A re-export of the same generation under new export options keeps it and raises options_revision instead. Connectors may be enabled at any point in a topic's life, so the first manifest a topic has need not be generation 1, and a first manifest supersedes nothing.

options_revision.description: The revision of the mounted connector and export-options configuration the bundle was assembled under. It is the second half of the ordering pair: the same approved generation re-exported after the operator changes what an export contains, or enables another connector, is newer material rather than a duplicate to ignore.

approval.description: Unapproved work is never exported. The approval is the operator's `publication_approval` decision about this exact source revision and content hash (P-5, G-13), checked where the manifest is stored.

approved_revision.description: Equal to source.revision by construction: an export is of the revision that was approved, not merely of work that carries an approval id. The DDL checks that the stored manifest's approved revision IS the row's source revision.

expected_connectors.description: The enabled connectors this export was committed for, keyed by connector id so one connector cannot appear twice with contradictory types. Enablement itself is mounted config. Every connector gets the same manifest and the same bundle; a connector's type decides how it writes, never what it is given.

implementation.description: Required for an extension connector: the module that implements it, packaged outside the core and baked into the image by a release, and the review that accepted it. An extension is engine-facing code, so it arrives by image release — never by an operator adding a name to mounted config (design review §6).

supersedes.description: The manifest this one replaces, with its ordering pair. Null when this is the topic's first manifest (including when connectors were enabled at a later generation).

tombstones.description: Entities removed or corrected relative to the superseded manifest; each connector acknowledges them, and a delivery that did not acknowledge them is not `delivered`.

allOf.description: Nothing to supersede means nothing to tombstone.

Generation 1 is the first approved revision: nothing of an earlier generation exists for it to supersede, only an earlier options revision of generation 1 itself. (The full pair comparison is the DDL's.)
